identity.real_world_identity_notes: British sports prototype built by Ginetta, developed from its LMP3 car with a carbon fibre monocoque and a 6,162 cc LS3 of about 575 bhp.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither.
The clutch is needed to pull away, which the drive established directly.
The source names the gearbox but not its shift mechanism, so the paddle actuation comes from the drive.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.ginetta-g58.20260816t150953718z-ea537c38 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the G58 and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives an X-Trac P1152 six-speed sequential gearbox, and the live drive selected six sequential gears with automatic cut and blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The guided drive that produced this record predates the rim-vocabulary merge and recorded the retired "gt-style" value. It is migrated to "gt-formula", which describes the same control-panel rim; the rim was not observed again.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential with one job left for your left foot, which is the clutch to pull away. After that it cuts the upshift and blips the downshift on its own.
